clue.text: Change made by Michael Butor

definitions.meaning: an alteration or adjustment to something
the French novelist Michel Butor wrote the 1957 novel La ..., here credited by title

explanation.surface: A remark that some alteration was the work of the French novelist Butor.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half names a book rather than defining a word: Butor's novel La Modification (in English, Second Thoughts) gives the answer's English form. The clue prints Michel as 'Michael'.
explanation.definitionFit: An alteration is a change, and the same word is the English form of Butor's novel's title.

clue.text: Novelist preparing for action

definitions.meaning: Olivia ... wrote the Balkan and Levant trilogies
a crew staffs the guns or the stations before a fight

explanation.surface: A writer getting ready for a battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Olivia Manning is a British novelist, and crewing the guns is the naval phrase for getting ready to fight.

clue.text: Pamela Frankenau's is proverbially better

parts.note: The proverb says the fiend you know is better than the one you don't

explanation.surface: Something belonging to the novelist Pamela Frankau is said, by proverb, to be the better option.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'better the devil you know' and Frankau's title The Devil We Know both point to the same word. The clue prints her name as 'Frankenau'.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb holds that a familiar evil fiend is preferable to an unknown one, and Frankau's title borrows it.

clue.text: Translation of Fraser oft attributed to Francis Brett Young

indicators.note: a translation turns words into another form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rendering of something by one Fraser, wrongly credited to the novelist Francis Brett Young.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Translation of' rearranges FRASER OFT. Far Forest (1936) is a novel by Francis Brett Young, so the title is fairly 'attributed' to him.
explanation.definitionFit: Far Forest is the title of a 1936 novel by the English writer Francis Brett Young, so the book is credited to him.

clue.text: Hughes's flier was also war reporter

definitions.meaning: Ted Hughes's 1970 poem sequence is about a black carrion bird
in old battle poetry the black carrion bird is the herald who brings news of slaughter, one of the beasts of battle

explanation.surface: Ted Hughes's bird was a war correspondent too.
explanation.definitionFit: Ted Hughes's poem cycle is named after the black bird, which in old heroic verse haunts battlefields and announces the carnage.

clue.text: Thomas's powerless treatment of Greene theme?

definitions.text: Thomas's powerless treatment of Greene theme?

parts.words: Thomas's powerless treatment of Greene theme?
parts.note: Graham Greene's novel The Power and ..., with the power taken away, leaves only its last two words, read as another writer's title

explanation.surface: A writer called Thomas handles a Graham Greene subject but without any strength.
explanation.walkthrough: Greene's title is The Power and the Glory; 'powerless' strips away the first half, leaving the closing phrase, presented as a work by a writer named Thomas.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking power out of Greene's title phrase leaves only its closing words, which also stand alone as a title.

clue.text: Abstract style originates only partly as realist tendency

indicators.note: where each word originates is its start, so the opening letters of the following words are taken

explanation.surface: A remark that an abstract art movement began, in part, as a realist trend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originates' takes the first letters of 'only partly as realist tendency'.
explanation.definitionFit: Op art is the 1960s abstract painting style built on optical illusions.

clue.text: Some extremely precious writing

parts.note: describes the highly mannered prose style named after John Lyly's Euphues

explanation.surface: A dismissive comment on a piece of overwrought prose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Precious' means affected or over-refined, not valuable: the style is named after Lyly's Euphues (1578), famous for its artificial ornament.
explanation.definitionFit: The style takes its name from Lyly's Euphues and means elaborately affected, ornamented prose.

clue.text: Something hidden from E. Phillips Oppenheim and Laurence Binyon

definitions.meaning: a thing kept out of sight or unknown to others

definitions.text: from E. Phillips Oppenheim and Laurence Binyon
definitions.meaning: both the thriller writer Oppenheim and the poet Binyon used this word in titles

explanation.surface: Something kept concealed from two Edwardian writers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' looks like 'kept from' in the surface, but it means 'written by': the second half names a title the two authors share.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything kept hidden is undisclosed, and the word was a title for both the spy novelist and the poet.

clue.text: Postponement sine die threatened by large corvid

definitions.meaning: putting something off with no date set, in effect for ever
the raven in Poe's poem The Raven croaks its single word as a threat

explanation.surface: An indefinite adjournment hangs under the menace of a big crow.
explanation.walkthrough: The corvid is Poe's Raven, whose one-word refrain forbids hope; sine die is Latin for 'without a day', i.e. postponed with no date fixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Postponing with no day set means not ever, and that refusal is the refrain of the bird in Poe's poem.

clue.text: Entertain artist's inspiration

definitions.meaning: to divert or make someone laugh
a goddess or person who inspires a creative artist, read as two words

explanation.surface: Divert the source of a painter's ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: To divert someone is to entertain them, and split as A MUSE it names a source of artistic inspiration.

clue.text: "Things — - — had ever bad success" (Henry VI Part 3)

parts.note: a line from Shakespeare's Henry VI Part 3 with a gap; the missing compound adjective means obtained dishonestly

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare quotation with a word missing, saying that some things never prosper.
explanation.walkthrough: The line in Henry VI Part 3 (II.ii) runs 'Things ill got had ever bad success'; the hyphenated word fills the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing words describe goods acquired by wrongful means, which the line says never prosper.

clue.text: Munitions manufacturer and collaborator produced dramatic results

definitions.meaning: an arrow-maker supplied the ammunition of the medieval archer
John ... co-wrote plays with Francis Beaumont and with Shakespeare

explanation.surface: An arms maker and his partner turned out a spectacular outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Munitions' means arrows here, and 'dramatic' is literal: the collaborator is the Jacobean playwright John Fletcher, Beaumont's partner.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrow-maker's trade name is also the surname of the Jacobean playwright who wrote plays jointly with Beaumont.

clue.text: Song he composed in land of plenty

indicators.note: music composed is put together, so these letters are assembled in a new order

explanation.surface: A man composes a song set in a rich country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' rearranges SONG HE.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Goshen is the fertile region of Egypt given to the Israelites, so the name means a place of abundance.

clue.text: Poliakoff and Potter are well-known ones

definitions.text: Poliakoff and Potter are well-known ones

parts.words: Poliakoff and Potter are well-known ones
parts.note: the playwright Stephen Poliakoff and the humorist Stephen Potter share a first name

explanation.surface: A statement that Poliakoff and Potter are famous examples of something.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites two surnames' common trade; the link is the shared first name, Stephen, made plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Both men bear the first name Stephen, so they are famous examples of people with that name.

clue.text: Engraving of laconic fieldsman

parts.note: a laconic remark is terse and wry, as is dry humour
point is a fielding position in cricket, square of the batsman on the off side

explanation.surface: A print depicting a terse cricket fielder.
explanation.walkthrough: POINT is a cricket fielding position close to the batsman on the off side.
explanation.definitionFit: Drypoint is an intaglio printmaking technique, scratching lines straight into a plate with a needle.

clue.text: Nursery rep, company?

definitions.meaning: a preschool group where young children are looked after
a repertory company is a troupe that puts on drama, read as two words

explanation.surface: A preschool that is also a repertory theatre troupe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rep' is short for repertory theatre, so the question mark asks you to split the answer as a drama troupe.
explanation.definitionFit: A preschool session for toddlers is a nursery, and split in two the word names a troupe that stages drama.

clue.text: How Oscar Wilde felt we should be, from laughing, reading of Little Nell's death

definitions.text: How Oscar Wilde felt we should be, from laughing, reading of Little Nell's death

parts.words: How Oscar Wilde felt we should be, from laughing, reading of Little Nell's death
parts.note: Wilde said one must have a heart of stone to read of Little Nell's death without laughing, so the eyes would be moist with mirth

explanation.surface: A recollection of Wilde's quip about Dickens's Little Nell.
explanation.walkthrough: Little Nell is the heroine of Dickens's The Old Curiosity Shop; Wilde's quip turns sentimental tears into tears of laughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Moist eyes come from tears, here tears of mirth rather than the sentimental weeping the phrase usually describes.

clue.text: His arrival and departure were booked in 1943

definitions.text: His arrival and departure were booked in 1943

parts.words: His arrival and departure were booked in 1943
parts.note: the novel Arrival and Departure was published in 1943 by the Hungarian-born author of Darkness at Noon

explanation.surface: A traveller's arrival and departure were reserved back in 1943.
explanation.walkthrough: 'booked' means put in a book, not reserved: Arrival and Departure is Arthur Koestler's 1943 novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Koestler wrote the 1943 novel Arrival and Departure, so his title was published, i.e. booked, that year.

clue.text: Composer is a different lady, OK?

indicators.note: the letters become a different arrangement, so the words that follow are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a woman, a different one, is all right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is a different' rearranges LADY OK.
explanation.definitionFit: Zoltán Kodály was a Hungarian composer and music educator.

clue.text: Dragon-killer no gentleman, getting a certain amount back

parts.note: a cad is a man who behaves dishonourably

indicators.note: back means the word for an amount is written backwards

parts.note: a sum is an amount of money

explanation.surface: A slayer of dragons proves a scoundrel when he gets some money returned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns SUM into MUS.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Cadmus killed the dragon guarding a spring before founding Thebes.

clue.text: "She came. And sang to me the whole / Of those three — that you made" (Tennyson)

definitions.text: She came. And sang to me the whole / Of those three — that you made

parts.words: She came. And sang to me the whole / Of those three — that you made
parts.note: lines from Tennyson's The Miller's Daughter with a gap; the missing word names units of verse

explanation.surface: A Tennyson quotation with a word missing, about a woman singing someone's verses.
explanation.walkthrough: The poem is Tennyson's The Miller's Daughter: she sang 'the whole / Of those three stanzas that you made'.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word is the plural for divisions of a poem, the verses she sang.

clue.text: Two notes added to any I composed for Hungarian pianist

parts.note: doh is the first note of the tonic sol-fa scale

indicators.note: 'to' puts one piece inside the other
set in order, so the following letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: n. is the standard abbreviation for a note, as in a footnote reference

explanation.surface: Two notes are added to a piece someone composed for a pianist from Hungary.
explanation.walkthrough: The two notes are DOH (sol-fa) and N (the abbreviation for a footnote); 'added to' puts them before ANY I, which 'composed' leaves in the order printed.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernő Dohnányi was a Hungarian pianist, composer and conductor.

clue.text: Scene of conflict in Shakespeare, naturally

indicators.note: in means the letters are found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A battle set in Shakespeare, of course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' picks the letters from inside 'shakespeARE NAturally'.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is a place where combat or contest happens, from the Roman amphitheatre.

clue.text: Character in Eliot drama, also found in saga that inspired it

indicators.note: found in means the letters are located inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A figure in a T. S. Eliot play also appears in the ancient story that inspired it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' takes the letters from 'sAGA THAt'. The play is Eliot's The Family Reunion, modelled on Aeschylus's Oresteia, the 'saga'.
explanation.definitionFit: Agatha is the aunt in Eliot's verse play The Family Reunion.

clue.text: Attempt by Charlotte M. Yonge

definitions.meaning: a try or test
the Victorian novelist Charlotte M. Yonge wrote The ... (1864), sequel to The Daisy Chain

explanation.surface: An effort made by the Victorian novelist Charlotte Yonge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' means 'written by': the Victorian novelist's book The Trial is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial is a test or try, and it is also the title of Yonge's 1864 novel.

clue.text: A French refusal for prolific writer

parts.note: non is French for no

explanation.surface: A French writer of many books turns something down.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'prolific writer' is Anonymous, credited with countless poems and ballads of unknown authorship.
explanation.definitionFit: Anonymous is credited with more works than any named author, so the abbreviation stands for a hugely productive writer.

clue.text: Weapon accompanying a lot at the Round Table

definitions.meaning: a long spear carried by a mounted knight

definitions.text: accompanying a lot at the Round Table
definitions.meaning: placed beside the word lot it makes the name of Arthur's foremost knight

explanation.surface: Arms carried by many of Arthur's knights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot' is the word LOT: put this weapon with it and you have Lancelot of the Round Table.
explanation.definitionFit: A lance is a knight's spear, and joined to 'lot' it gives Lancelot, Arthur's best knight.

clue.text: American reportedly with zero intelligence is in fact a brilliant playwright

parts.note: Yank is a colloquial word for an American
O looks like zero

indicators.note: said aloud, the word for intelligence matches the ending of the surname

parts.note: wits are mental sharpness

explanation.surface: An American said to have no brains is actually a gifted dramatist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' makes WITS sound like WITZ. Susan Yankowitz is an American playwright; 'brilliant' plays on the wits.
explanation.definitionFit: Susan Yankowitz is an American dramatist known for Night Sky and work with the Open Theater.

clue.text: Catalan dance might be Paul's in Delacroix subject

parts.note: the sardana is the circle dance of Catalonia

indicators.note: might be suggests the letters could form something else, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the name Paul with the possessive s counted as a letter

explanation.surface: A Catalan dance turns out to belong to Paul, in a painting by Delacroix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might be' rearranges PAULS into PALUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Delacroix painted The Death of Sardanapalus (1827), showing the legendary Assyrian king amid his destroyed treasures.
